title: Sheafified tensor sections preserve cokernels
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Define $T_X$ on every module $F$ by sheafifying the presheaf $U\mapsto\operatorname{ULift}\Gamma(U,u^*F)$, with the normalized tensor restrictions [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-presheaf-functorial] and with maps $\varphi\mapsto\Gamma(U,u^*\varphi)$; their naturality is [lem-sc-etale-tensor-sections-map-naturality]. Then $T_X$ preserves colimits of parallel pairs, in particular categorical cokernels. For quasi-coherent $F$, its value is canonically the lifted specified tensor-sections sheaf [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module].

source.place: Lemma 35.8.5 (2); see also Tag 03FH (1), and the original additive comparison Step 2

proof.text: Construct the module-variable functor using componentwise tensor-pullback maps; the named naturality theorem supplies its natural-transformation proof. Its identity, composition, and additive laws follow from those of tensor pullback, and its coefficients are lifted before sheafification.

Tensor pullback preserves cokernels because it is left adjoint. On each etale object, sections of the resulting module cokernel locally lift to the middle module on a Zariski cover; sections mapping to zero locally come from the source module. These covers are etale covers, so sheafification gives the cokernel on the etale site. Equivalently apply the ringed-site pullback description of Stacks 070S(2), which is right exact, and then forget to abelian sheaves.

The functor is additive, so a coequalizer of two maps is the cokernel of their difference. Thus preservation of cokernels implies preservation of all parallel-pair colimits. The additive universe lift preserves colimits.
